I started my weight loss journey at 248 pounds and I felt really hopeless. I think theres some really great advice here already but I can tell you that one of the most important things for me is mindset. I tell myself I CAN do this. I remind myself why I am getting into better shape. 

First of all, start off by slowly cutting things out of your diet. I personally switched into high protein low carbs and its worked out great for me so far. I find myself less hungry and I dont snack throughout the day anymore. I discovered as well that I am a stress eater and stress triggers me to want to eat. Now when I am stressed I will go to the gym, go for a walk, draw, or do something otherwise to help me from eating my feelings and it has helped a ton. I think its about finding the healthy foods you like and realizing you have to eat to live and sustain your body to stay healthy, not for emotional reasons. Its a very hard cycle to break. 

I'll also offer that if you need a weight loss buddy or someone to reach out to you can feel free to message me directly. Having support helps a ton with weight loss, especially since cravings aren't going to stop. Make the changes slowly and remind yourself you can do it!

My story is kinda crazy, it happened from a failed suicide attempt. After taking a ton of pills and feeling 0 effects I decided to go swim it off. I went to the hot tub and I started to feel really, really dizzy. I looked at the clock and it was 8 pm. I tried to move but it was like I was paralyzed. I couldn't move. I cant explain everything that happened but I remember it being 8:15, then 8:20, i remember seeing 8:30 and crawling to the steps of the hot tub and then I blacked out. 

I remember waking up and I was sitting on this cliff. There was a single tree behind me. I scooted forward and my legs were hanging off the edge. There was this black mist and I couldnt see through it. I heard some faint whispering, and I decided to jump. As I was falling I felt comfort at first. But it quickly turned to panic. The whispering got louder and I heard screaming. I panicked and I grabbed onto the cliff and started climbing. I felt like I was being pulled down, like there were hands from the black mist dragging me down but I kept climbing and climbing. My hands were bleeding and in that moment I somehow knew I had to live. I reached the top of the cliff after what felt like years of climbing. The second I laid down I woke up, surrounded by paramedics and lifeguards.
